subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Equivalence Partitioning
description: A quick win: understand Equivalence Partitioning.

hook.text: A field accepts ages 18–65. Do you test every number from 18 to 65? No. You test one from each group.

buildup.text: Equivalence partitioning divides inputs into groups where every value in a group should behave the same.

discovery.text: If age 25 passes, ages 18–65 should all pass. One test per partition covers the entire group.

twist.text: The power is in invalid partitions too. Testing age -1, 0, or 200 catches missing validation rules.

climax.text: Equivalence partitioning cuts test cases dramatically—from thousands of values to a handful of smart ones.

punchline.text: One value per group. Smart sampling beats brute force.

quiz.question: What does equivalence partitioning do?
options: Groups inputs where values should behave identically
